title: feat(spec): an `oauth2` `authorization_code` connector instance can take its OAuth client from the installer — `clientSource: 'installer'`
body:
<!-- claude-projects-attribution: {"github_login":"os-steve"} -->
_Requested by **Steve** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_01FdL1XeUyvVNxLreh3F4Qi9?thread=cmsg_01FdL1XeUyvVNxLreh3F4Qi97JUcgFYCr7uuKzrKbe2paU)_
Fixes #28864

Clause-②: yes (widening)
Metadata-protocol: added
Skills-docs: follow-up owed — `skills/objectstack-automation/references/integration-recipes.md` (its e-signature recipe pins `clientId: 'objectstack-prod'`, the publisher-owned client ruling 6566728470 rules out for a listing) and `content/docs/automation/connectors.mdx` (the `oauth2` section). Both should teach `clientSource: 'installer'` once the server slice (#28866) serves it: taught today, the key sends an author to an instance the service holds degraded. The skill file is governed (Tier H).
Ruling-ref: 6566728470

## 维护者速读

- 改了什么:`oauth2` 的 `authorization_code` 连接器实例新增可选键 `clientSource: 'installer'`,声明「OAuth 客户端由安装方自带」:每个部署的管理员自己到厂商处登记客户端(回调填本部署的地址),把 client id 和 secret 填在连接上；定义里不写 `clientId`、`credentialRef`,两者同写会被拒。ADR-0143 D2.1 追加一条修订说明。
- 为什么改:厂商只认登记过回调地址的客户端，而回调地址每个部署都不同；包里写死的 `clientId` 只在发布者登记过的部署上能连上。#28702 裁决 B(「同意」)要求开源版 OAuth 应用不带官方客户端、由安装方自带,DocuSign 应用等这一步。
- 风险与回滚:纯放宽，不写新键的实例解析结果完全不变，包里写 `clientId` 的私有应用照旧可用。服务端还不读这个键(#28866 再做):非 MCP 实例声明它会被标为降级，绝不会无客户端发请求。回滚即撤掉本 PR。
- 先看:`packages/spec/src/integration/connector.zod.ts` 的 ADR-0143 D2.1 规则块(两处 `installerClient`);`packages/spec/src/shared/connector-auth.zod.ts` 的 `clientSource` 与上方 docblock;`docs/adr/0143-outbound-connector-auth-is-open-tier.md` D2 末尾的新修订说明。
- 两分钟验证:`pnpm --filter @objectstack/spec exec vitest run src/integration/connector-auth-grant-kinds.test.ts`,应看到 29 条全过(其中 9 条是本次新增)。
- 需要你做的:批准本 PR,连同新公开键名 `clientSource`(值 `'installer'`)。ADR 受管，合并要等你的批准。

## What changes

- **`clientSource` on the `authorization_code` instance shape** (`ConnectorInstanceOAuth2AuthorizationCodeAuthSchema`, `@objectstack/spec` and `@objectstack/spec/integration`): an optional closed enum with one member, `'installer'`. The administrator of each deployment registers their own client with the vendor, against that deployment's callback, and enters its id and secret on the instance's connection. The definition then names no client and no secret.
  - A `clientId` beside it is refused at publish, `custom @ auth.clientId`, on every provider: the definition would name two clients. The rule is in `DeclarativeConnectorEntrySchema`'s ADR-0143 D2.1 block (claim amended to include it), beside the other client-key rules.
  - Off `provider: 'mcp'` over http, the installer form no longer needs `clientId`. `tokenUrl` and `authorizationUrl` are still required there: the installer owns the client, not the vendor's authorization server.
  - A `credentialRef` without `clientId` stays refused at `auth.credentialRef` by the shape's existing `dependentRequired`; its message now names the installer form.
  - On `grant: 'client_credentials'` the key is refused as an unknown key with a guidance entry: that grant keeps no connection record, so there is nowhere to enter a client.
  - The `clientId` row of each grant now says only where else a client may come from for that grant (`oauth2SharedShape(clientIdNote)`).
- **What the D2.1 block accepted before and after**, for the seat: before, an `oauth2` entry off MCP-over-http was refused at `auth.clientId` whenever `clientId` was absent. After, the same holds unless the entry is `authorization_code` with `clientSource: 'installer'`. A new refusal fires only for an entry that carries `clientSource`, a key every earlier input was refused for (`unrecognized_keys`). No input that parsed before is refused now, and no input refused before is accepted unless it carries `clientSource`.
- **ADR-0143 D2.1 amendment** (append-only, dated 2026-11-02, under D2 after the 2026-10-31 note): why, what the variant carries, where the installer's client lives (the connection record's per-connection client record, beside a dynamically registered client; D3's persisted list grows by it), why a packaged `clientId` is kept, `client_credentials` unchanged, and the per-account API host left as a follow-up.
- **Generated:** `content/docs/references/integration/connector.mdx` (regenerated), `packages/spec/authorable-surface/integration.json` gains `ConnectorInstanceOAuth2AuthorizationCodeAuth:clientSource`. No export moved (`check:api-surface` green). `docs/adr/README.md` does not move (`adr-index` OK).
- **Changeset:** `.changeset/28864-oauth2-installer-client.md`, `@objectstack/spec: minor`.

### Forced test edits

- `packages/spec/src/integration/connector-credential-redaction.test.ts`: the fail-closed census `DECLARED_NOT_A_SECRET` lists `clientSource`. The census reds on any newly declared instance-auth key until it is confirmed not to be a secret; `clientSource` is a closed enum value.

## Why

Ruling 6566728470 on #28702 (letter B, maintainer 「同意」 2026-11-02): an open-edition OAuth connector app ships no ObjectStack-owned `clientId` or secret, and the administrator of each deployment registers their own integration key against that deployment's callback and enters it on the connection. Today the client is a literal of the definition (`clientId`), so whoever publishes the package fixes it, and the vendor's consent page refuses it on every deployment whose callback that client's owner never registered. This is the spec slice; #28866 (server) and #28869 (ui) are `Blocked-by` it, and #28277 (DocuSign) waits on all three.

## Tests

`packages/spec/src/integration/connector-auth-grant-kinds.test.ts`, a new describe with 9 tests, each refusal pinned by `code @ path`:

- CONTROL accepts: the installer form with endpoints on `openapi`; the installer form on `mcp` over http with no endpoints; a packaged `clientId` without `clientSource` (the accept set does not move).
- Refusals: `clientId` beside `clientSource` (alone, with `credentialRef`, and on `mcp` over http) at `auth.clientId`; `credentialRef` with the installer form at `auth.credentialRef`; the endpoints still required off MCP-over-http (`auth.tokenUrl`, `auth.authorizationUrl`, and no `auth.clientId`); an unknown value at `auth.clientSource` (`invalid_value`); `clientSource` on `client_credentials` (`unrecognized_keys`).
- The parsed installer definition carries exactly `authorizationUrl`, `clientSource`, `grant`, `scopes`, `tokenUrl`, `type`: no client, no secret.

## Acceptance notes

- **The packaged-`clientId` choice: kept, for private apps.** Measured on `origin/main` `76bf6c50`: no example, packaged app or `connector-*` source authors an `oauth2` instance; the authors are test fixtures (spec, service-automation, connector-openapi, lint, ui app-shell), the docs example in `content/docs/automation/connectors.mdx`, the skill recipe above, and ADR-0143 Q3's HubSpot case (a pre-registered client on an MCP server without dynamic registration). Refusing a packaged `clientId` would refuse every one of those inputs, a narrowing beside this widening, and the schema cannot tell a private app (whose author registers every callback) from a listing. So it stays accepted, and the ruling's listing rule is held where listings are reviewed (suggested carrier: #27293).
- **Why the `clientId` exclusion is on the entry, not the shape.** The closed list in `shared/refinement-projection.ts` has no arm for "this key excludes that one", so a shape-level `.refine` would add a dropped-refinement site to every published schema that embeds the auth shape. The entry's `superRefine` is already marked as not stated (`integration/DeclarativeConnectorEntry` `out` in `dropped-refinements.baseline.json`), holds the other provider-dependent client-key rules, and is what both authoring doors parse. A standalone `ConnectorInstanceAuthSchema.parse` accepts the pair; no runtime door parses the auth shape alone.
- **Interim, until #28866.** The automation service does not read `clientSource`. Off MCP, `oauth2NotServableReason` (`packages/services/service-automation/src/plugin.ts`) holds such an instance degraded for a missing `clientId`, never called without a client. On `mcp` over http, `mcpDiscoveryServerUrl` sees `clientId` undefined and runs the MCP authorization flow, registering a client where the server allows it. The changeset says both.
- **Server-slice seams** (for #28866, read on this head): `plugin.ts#oauth2NotServableReason` and `#mcpDiscoveryServerUrl` (treat the installer form as supplying the client), `#mcpAuthorizationClient` (`kept.registered === (auth.clientId === undefined)`, and no registration for the installer form), the connection door's begin step (take the client id and secret), `oauth2-grant/grant-handle.ts#createOAuth2GrantHandle` (`declaredClient`), and `sys-connector-connection.object.ts`'s `registered_client` description. UI slice (#28869): `ui/packages/app-shell/src/views/setup/connectorConnections.ts` and `ConnectorConnectionsPage.tsx` (the form, with the deployment's redirect URI).
- **DocuSign production host.** Not measured (the container cannot reach the vendor). The ADR note leaves a per-account API host to a follow-up; endpoints stay in the definition, sandbox first.

## Verification

All readings on head `23acaa6a` (this branch with `origin/main` `b15b634c` merged in) unless a line says otherwise; every heavy run went through `os-verify-lock.sh`, whose `VERDICT command-exit` line is quoted.

- `pnpm --filter @objectstack/spec test`: Test Files 789 passed (789), Tests 23324 passed, 1 todo. VERDICT command-exit 0.

- `connector.zod.ts`, the relaxation `if (entry.auth.clientId === undefined && !installerClient) {` → without `&& !installerClient`: 4 failed | 25 passed (the openapi CONTROL accept, the `credentialRef` refusal's single issue, the endpoints-still-required list, the declared-keys pin). Restored: blob == HEAD.
- Reverse type verification: a probe in `packages/services/service-automation` typed `ConnectorInstanceAuth` from `@objectstack/spec/integration`: `clientSource: 'installer'` compiles, `clientSource: 'publisher'` is TS2322 (`'"publisher"' is not assignable to type '"installer"'`), so the consumer reads the rebuilt `.d.ts`. Probe deleted; `git status` clean.
